specs.anchorText: There are three, and they fail at different time scales
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette: a three-rung ladder climbing upward to the right, each rung wider and a little harder to reach than the last, with a small cartoon film strip climbing it. On the lowest, nearest rung, a single frame jitters with tiny vibration lines and a couple of shimmering dust motes (a quick, twitchy little failure). On the middle rung, a friendly cartoon dog slowly morphs into a slightly different dog across a few faint ghost outlines, looking confused about its own identity. On the top, hardest rung, a small ball floats absurdly uphill against a slope while a puzzled cartoon Isaac-Newton-style apple refuses to fall, gently breaking physics. The rungs get visibly steeper and trickier toward the top to show growing difficulty. The style should be friendly and approachable, like a comic strip or an XKCD-inspired infographic, expressive and uncluttered, on a clean white background with generous margins. Suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image. The humor should be gentle and immediately understandable. Keep the composition simple and focused on one clear visual metaphor: the longer the time scale of a failure, the deeper the fix it demands.
specs.alt: A three-rung ladder rising left to right where each rung is harder to climb. The bottom rung shows a single frame jittering with vibration lines (flicker), the middle rung shows a cartoon dog slowly morphing into a different dog across ghost outlines (identity drift), and the top rung shows a ball rolling uphill and an apple refusing to fall (motion incoherence). The increasing steepness maps the three temporal-consistency failures to growing time scale and growing difficulty.
specs.caption: The longer the time scale of a failure, the deeper the fix it demands: flicker is an architecture bug, identity drift is a context-length bug, and motion incoherence is a world-knowledge bug.

specs.anchorText: named for the two-faced Roman god
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette: a friendly cartoon art-critic character (a small floating monocle-and-clipboard creature representing a frozen 2D image critic) circling all the way around a sculptor's turntable that holds a clay animal head. From every angle the critic visited, it has happily stamped a little green check-mark and a smiling-face badge, so the sculptor has obediently added a face on the front AND a second face on the back of the head, leaving a comical two-faced creature. The sculptor robot looks bewildered, holding its tools, realizing nobody told the critic that heads are supposed to have a back. Show a couple of curved motion arrows indicating the critic walked around the turntable. The style should be friendly and approachable, like a comic strip or an XKCD-inspired infographic, expressive and uncluttered, on a clean white background with generous margins. Suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image. The humor should be gentle and immediately understandable. Keep the composition simple and focused on one clear visual metaphor: a viewpoint-blind 2D critic approving a face from every angle produces a two-faced 3D object.
specs.alt: A floating cartoon art-critic with a monocle circles a turntable holding a clay animal head, leaving smiling approval stamps at every angle. Because it judged each view independently, the bewildered sculptor robot has built a face on both the front and the back of the head, illustrating the Janus problem where a viewpoint-agnostic 2D diffusion prior grows duplicate faces during score distillation.
specs.caption: A 2D critic that grades every angle as if it were a headshot will happily approve a face on the back of the head too; the fix is handing it a compass so it knows which side it is looking at.

specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette: a friendly cartoon car-agent peacefully asleep in a tiny bed, wearing a sleeping cap, with a big soft dreamy thought-bubble cloud above it. Inside the dream bubble, the same little car is happily practicing on a toy-like driving course, gently bumping into puffy cloud-walls and cloud-cones over and over without any harm, with a few faint repeated ghost-trails showing it has tried many times. Outside the bubble, a single small real road waits quietly with one real cone on it, to show that real practice is rare and the dream is where most learning happens. A small recycling-style loop arrow connects the real road back up to the dream to suggest occasional refreshing of the dream from reality. The style should be friendly and approachable, like a comic strip or an XKCD-inspired infographic, expressive and uncluttered, on a clean white background with generous margins. Suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image. The humor should be gentle and immediately understandable. Keep the composition simple and focused on one clear visual metaphor: a world-model agent trains cheaply inside its own dream and only rarely touches the costly real world.
specs.alt: A cartoon car-agent sleeps in a tiny bed under a large dream bubble, and inside the dream it practices driving over and over on a soft cloud course, harmlessly bumping cloud-walls with faint repeated ghost-trails. Outside the bubble a single real road with one cone waits, and a small loop arrow refreshes the dream from reality, depicting how a world model lets a policy train in cheap imagined rollouts and only occasionally act in the expensive real world.
specs.caption: An agent does not need to crash a thousand real cars; it crashes a thousand imaginary ones in a dream it built from watching, and the world model's quality is the ceiling on how well that practice transfers.

specs.anchorText: spends its capacity on what is predictable and structural
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette: a calm, wise little robot fortune-teller sitting before a windy tree, declining to do a hard task and choosing an easy wise one instead. On one side, a frantic exhausted robot with many arms tries to draw every single individual leaf swirling in the wind onto a chaotic cluttered canvas and is clearly losing (crumpled papers, sweat drops). On the other side, the calm robot simply holds up a small clean card showing a single simple tree silhouette icon, serenely predicting that the tree will still be a tree, ignoring the unpredictable leaf chaos. A gentle dividing element separates wasteful pixel-detail prediction from efficient abstract prediction. The style should be friendly and approachable, like a comic strip or an XKCD-inspired infographic, expressive and uncluttered, on a clean white background with generous margins. Suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image. The humor should be gentle and immediately understandable. Keep the composition simple and focused on one clear visual metaphor: predicting abstract structure beats wasting capacity rendering irreducibly unpredictable detail.
specs.alt: On the left a frantic many-armed robot exhausts itself trying to draw every swirling leaf of a windy tree onto a cluttered canvas and fails. On the right a calm robot serenely holds a card with a simple tree silhouette, predicting only that the tree will still be a tree. The contrast illustrates JEPA predicting abstract structure in representation space instead of wasting capacity rendering unpredictable pixel detail.
specs.caption: Predicting the exact dance of every leaf is a losing game; predicting that the tree will still be a tree is the part worth knowing, which is why JEPA throws the pixel decoder away.

specs.alt: A two-panel cartoon: a player in a generated room first faces a crisp doorway, then after a turn-around arrow looks back to find the same spot has quietly become a window while the room edges go slightly melty. specs.caption: A neural game engine has the memory of a goldfish with excellent eyesight: the world is gorgeous while you look at it and starts renegotiating with reality the moment you look away.
